3f97a947aaf9a43188f9edea4fb0cc1b863bd50f.content:
{
"Testing": "The systematic process of evaluating software to verify that it behaves as expected and to identify defects, ensuring both correctness and quality.",
"Software Correctness": "The property of software that indicates it behaves according to its specifications and produces the expected results for given inputs.",
"Software Quality": "The degree to which software meets specified requirements and user expectations, encompassing attributes such as reliability, maintainability, and performance.",
"Unit Test": "A test that verifies the behavior of an individual component or function in isolation from the rest of the system.",
"Integration Test": "A test that verifies multiple components work correctly together, validating the interactions and interfaces between them.",
"End-to-End Test": "A test that validates complete user workflows by exercising the entire application stack from start to finish, simulating real-world usage.",
"Component": "A discrete, modular unit of software, such as a class, function, or module, that performs a specific role within a larger system.",
"User Workflow": "A sequence of actions a user performs to accomplish a specific goal within an application, often used as the basis for end-to-end testing.",
"Mock": "A test double that simulates the behavior of a real dependency, allowing tests to verify interactions and isolate the code under test.",
"Stub": "A test double that provides predefined, canned responses to calls made during tests, used to control the indirect inputs of the code under test.",
"Dependency": "An external component, module, or service that a piece of code relies on to function, which may be replaced with mocks or stubs during testing.",
"Canned Response": "A predefined, fixed output returned by a stub or mock when invoked, used to simulate dependency behavior in a controlled manner.",
"Test-Driven Development": "A software development methodology in which tests are written before the corresponding implementation code, guiding design and ensuring testability.",
"Implementation": "The actual code that realizes the functionality specified by requirements or tests, as opposed to specifications or test cases.",
"Code Coverage": "A metric that measures the proportion of source code executed by a test suite, used to assess the thoroughness of testing.",
"Test": "A procedure or piece of code designed to verify that software behaves as expected under specified conditions."
}
